A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAM/CMIC research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V4 reports original compression experiments on Kodak, Tecnick and CLIC, component ablations, receptive-field visualizations and training-stability results.

after.justification: V5 retains those original results and adds baseline comparisons, MambaIRv2-style component experiments, diagnostic visualizations and GPU latency measurements.

M1.justification: V5 explicitly constructs the prompt dictionary as U=A([c1;...;cK]), using a learned projection of clustering centroids. V4 describes U as differentiably learned but leaves its parameterization unspecified, so the PDFs do not establish whether this changes the prompt generator or discloses its existing construction. The backbone, clustering, scan and losses otherwise match.

E1.justification: Both versions train on Flickr2W and evaluate natural-image compression on Kodak, Tecnick and CLIC. The additional analyses use retained image coverage; discussing and adapting MambaIRv2 does not introduce a super-resolution task.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated HPCM, MLICv2, DCAE and LALIC comparisons while retaining previous baselines. Appendix A.13 also introduces two MambaIRv2-style comparison variants: a standalone prompt dictionary and a classification head combined with that dictionary. This substantially broadens the comparison methods.

E3.justification: The main training and benchmark settings remain unchanged. V5 adds a single-layer input-to-output ERF diagnostic explicitly using soft clustering, component-replacement controls in A.13, and encoding/decoding timing on RTX3090 alongside A100 measurements in A.14.

E4.justification: Figure 9 adds single-layer ERF comparisons isolating CTP and GPP effects. Appendix A.13, Table 9 and Figures 19–21 add substantial tests of dictionary construction, classification-head routing and semantic cluster structure. Existing component, cluster-count and stability analyses remain; the Kodim08 reconstruction case is removed.

E5.justification: Appendix A.8 and Figure 18 retain the same training-stability evidence for seeds 1024 and 16. Cluster statistics in Table 5 are unchanged, and v5 introduces no new run-count, confidence-interval, significance-test or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 1 entries change the Kodak ranking: MLICv2 reports -16.16% BD-rate versus CMIC's unchanged -15.91%. Table 9 adds two variant-result rows, Table 10 adds encoding and RTX3090 timings, and new figures add diagnostic findings. A.3.2 revises CAM-SCCTX decoding latency from 0.513 to 0.471 seconds. The Kodim08 reconstruction results are removed.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 adds the explicit mathematical definition U=A([c1;...;cK]), formally linking prompt vectors to clustering centroids. The existing rate-distortion loss, clustering/EMA algorithm, SSM dynamics and entropy-model equations otherwise remain equivalent. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: content-adaptive permutation, global-prior prompting and efficient CMIC compression. The headline BD-rate savings and state-of-the-art claims remain unchanged; the dictionary terminology is refined without otherwise changing these claims' scope.

C2.justification: V5 adds interpretations connecting the new ERFs and MambaIRv2-style comparisons to non-causality and semantic redundancy modeling. A.3.2 now acknowledges modest high-resolution benefits and future potential for CAM-based entropy modeling. Its general limitation concerning small benefits versus latency costs already existed in v4.

D1.justification: V5 specifies the centroid-to-prompt projection and construction of the new comparison variants. It also names a planned code repository and promises code/checkpoints upon acceptance, replacing the generic future-release statement. Existing training settings and VTM commands remain; the PDFs do not establish actual artifact availability.

R1.justification: MambaIRv2 was already cited, but v5 explicitly credits its attentive state-space equation and adds extensive motivation, design and experimental comparisons in A.13. New Section 2.3 develops content-adaptive positioning, including Routing Transformer and Adaptive Token Dictionary. This substantially sharpens the relationship to closely related work.

P1.justification: V5 makes targeted wording and terminology revisions, adds Section 2.3 and appendix subsections, and includes acknowledgment, ethics, reproducibility and LLM-use statements. The overall narrative structure and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 9, Figures 19–21 and Tables 9–10 substantially extend the visual presentation, while Table 1 gains four rows. Some CMIC panels are reused within new comparative figures. V4's Kodim08 Figure 13 is removed; other figures are retained with renumbering, relocation and limited labeling changes.

improvement.justification: V5 strengthens evaluation through recent baselines, targeted MambaIRv2-style controls and two-GPU latency measurements, while improving attribution and prompt-construction detail. These provide a limited net quality gain. However, Section 4.3 retains its broad outperformance claim even though the expanded Table 1 shows MLICv2 beating CMIC on Kodak, leaving the narrative insufficiently qualified.
